content:
zoe: quick heads-up — sampleapp ruby matrix is flaking on jruby/windows again, failing during `extconf.rb` compile. Repro locally with jruby 9.4 on Windows WSL.

zoe: error here: ```
checking for ruby/thread.h... no
In file included from sample_ext.c:1:
fatal error: ruby/thread.h: No such file or directory
 #include "ruby/thread.h"
         ^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
*** Compile failed -- exit code 1
```

pat: yeah that's the native extension assuming MRI headers. We intended the sample app to demonstrate the SDK (pure ruby call), not native extensions — looks like the platform gem got pulled in.

lee: suggestion: change the sampleapp Gemfile to `gem 'redwood-sdk', platforms: [:ruby]` and add a Gemfile.lock entry to prevent Windows platform gems from being resolved in CI. Alternatively add a pure-ruby fallback file in `lib/redwood/fallback.rb` that stubs out the native bits during CI.

zoe: both sounds good. I prefer Gemfile fix + a line in the sample README about JRuby limitations. Less code churn.

pat: I'll open a tiny PR to constrain the platform and add `BUNDLE_FORCE_RUBY_PLATFORM=1` to the jruby CI job. Also include a comment in the CI YAML referencing ticket DX-454 so it isn't removed later.

ci-bot: job failed 2: compile-native-exts (jruby-windows) — https://ci.redwood/job/7732 :x:

lee: one more note: when we switch to forcing ruby platform, add a smoke test that runs `ruby samples/ruby/run_sample.rb` under JRuby to ensure behavior parity (no native ext required). Keeps us honest.

zoe: agreed. I'll add the smoke command to the job. Thanks — will watch PR. :thumbsup:
